newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir separatists observe general strike.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir separatists observe general strike.

text.p: Shops and businesses shut down in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir's summer capital, on Sunday in a strike called by separatists to mark the 49th anniversary of the arrival of Indian troops in the Himalayan state.
On October 27, 1947, Indian troops landed in Kashmir, over which India and Pakistan, which disputes the region, have since fought three wars.

After partition of the sub-continent at the time of its independence from Britain in 1947, a Hindu ruler of independent Kashmir, facing the threat of an invasion from Pakistani Pathan tribesmen, hastily signed an instrument of accession to India in return for military aid.
Kashmir's leading separatist coalition called Sunday's strike urging people to observe a day of mourning.

"October 27 is the most unfortunate day for Kashmiris when Indian occupational forces landed in Kashmir," said a statement of the All Parties' Hurriyat Conference, which bands together some 30 religious and political separatist groups.
Most streets were deserted except for security patrols. Sunday is usually a normal business day in troubled Kashmir.

Over a dozen militant groups have been fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir, the only Moslem-majority state in mainly Hindu India, since 1990, when simmering discontent turned into a separatist rebellion.
The Indian Defence Ministry marks October 27 as "Infantry Day."
"Almost fifty years later, the queen of battle continues its selfless crusade against Pakistan-sponsored militancy in the Kashmir valley," a defence department statement said in Srinagar on Sunday.
India accuses Islamabad of arming and training separatist guerrillas. Pakistan says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the six-year-old rebellion in the state.

The latest casualties came late on Saturday when separatist guerrillas fired rockets at a house in Baramulla, 55 km (34 miles) north of Srinagar, killing five members of a pro-government militia group.
